# TM-4 demo set: two synthetic resumes

Both files here are **synthetic**. The people, employers, email addresses and phone
numbers are invented: emails use `example.com`, phone numbers use the 555-01xx range
reserved for fiction, employers are Microsoft's fictional sample companies, and neither
resume links any real account. They are test inputs, not results.

They are generated by `tests/fixtures/make_fixtures.py` (data `DEMO_KEYWORD_STUFFED` and
`DEMO_SUPPORT_OPS`), so they can be rebuilt byte for byte:

    nlp-engine/venv/Scripts/python tests/fixtures/make_fixtures.py

The demo job they are written against is the "dev" job of `tests/fixtures/manifest.json`
(`jds/dev.txt`; required: python, sql, postgresql, docker, git, rest api; preferred:
react, redis, aws, kubernetes).

| File | Candidate (invented) | What it is for | Expected in the demo |
|---|---|---|---|
| `demo_keyword_stuffed.pdf` | Casey Brightwater | Lists every skill of the demo job, several times, and little else: one vague job line and no evidence. No GitHub link. | Scores low and stays unverified: the claims have no GitHub evidence and nothing to back them. |
| `demo_support_ops.pdf` | Teodor Halloway | A support and operations engineer (ServiceNow, Jira, ITIL, Nagios, Active Directory, Windows Server, with SQL, PostgreSQL, Python scripting and Git) written as believable experience. No GitHub link. | Partly verified after the assessment: no GitHub evidence, but the claimed skills the job shares can be confirmed by the assessment. |

The third demo candidate is the owner's own resume with the `anthonyjennis` GitHub
account. He uploads it himself; it is never committed, copied into the repo or pasted
anywhere. Image-only input keeps using fixture `f6_image_only.pdf`.

Since card R-21 (`nlp-engine@2.2.0`) the support resume parses to python, powershell,
postgresql, git, linux, servicenow, jira, itil, nagios, active directory, windows server,
group policy and sql (before R-21: python, postgresql, git, linux and sql only). The
keyword-stuffed resume parses to python, react, postgresql, redis, aws, docker,
kubernetes, git, sql, rest and api, unchanged by R-21.
